A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
users’ decision to disclose on wearable devices is driven by both the perceived benefits of the devices as well as their privacy calculus.
privacy calculus is a significant predictor of self-disclosure, but it is moderated by the benefit structure of wearable devices.
users’ privacy calculus and benefit perceptions are key factors that motivate them to disclose, and continue to use, wearable devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decision to self-disclose on wearable devices is not a binary decision, but rather a continuous process.
users’ self-disclosure on wearables is not a one-time decision but a dynamic process that is affected by both privacy calculus and benefit perception.
privacy calculus plays a critical role in shaping users’ self-disclosure on the wearable devices.
